Dein Verantwortungsbereich umfasst die strategische Überwachung, das Leistungsmanagement, die Teamführung und die Zusammenarbeit mit funktionsübergreifenden Teams. Hierfür wirst Du eng mit dem Head of Operations sowie Ärzten und Fachkräften vor Ort arbeiten und netzwerken. Wachstum durch Standortentwicklung vorantreiben: Du siehst Wachstumschancen in Deiner Region und erkennst sie frühzeitig, um sie gewinnbringend zu nutzen. Du wirst durch effektive Marketing- und Werbestrategien zur Steigerung des Patientenaufkommens in enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Marketingteam beitragen. Dein Ziel ist es, einen Ausbau des Marktanteils zu erreichen. Du wirst zusammenarbeiten mit Einem starken Operationsteam, bestehend aus vielen Ex-Beratern (Bain, BCG, Roland Berger, Oliver Wyman). Leitenden Angestellten und Führungskräften bei Sanoptis, darunter der Head of Operations und das Führungsteam, das für klinische Innovation und hervorragende Dienstleistungen verantwortlich ist. Renommierten Spezialisten und führenden Experten auf dem Gebiet der Augenheilkunde. Einem engagierten und qualifizierten Team von medizinischen Fachkräften und Assistenzärzten. Interdisziplinären Teams in unserem gesamten Netzwerk, einschließlich Technologieexperten, die an den neuesten Fortschritten in der augenmedizinischen Behandlung und digitalen Gesundheitslösungen arbeiten. Dein Profil überzeugt durch Einschlägige Berufserfahrung in einem anspruchsvollen Umfeld, z. B. in der Strategieberatung (McKinsey, Bain, BCG o.Ä.) oder in ähnlich schnelllebigen Unternehmen. Die nachgewiesene Fähigkeit, Geschäfts- und Finanzanalysen auf Führungsebene zu erstellen und zu kommunizieren. Du erstellst Analysen akribisch und detailorientiert. Unternehmerisches Denken mit der Fähigkeit, große Verantwortung zu übernehmen und Problemlösungen unabhängig voranzutreiben. Eine eigenständige Arbeitsweise mit wenig Anleitung ist essenziell. Nachgewiesene Erfolge im Umgang mit Interessensgruppen, einschließlich der Fähigkeit, ohne formale Autorität Einfluss zu nehmen und Dir eine wichtige Rolle bei der Entscheidungsfindung zu sichern. Du besitzt die Fähigkeit, auch in schwierigen Situationen Konflikte konstruktiv zu lösen und Durchsetzungsstärke zu behalten. Ausgeprägte Fähigkeiten im Bereich Organisation und Prozessmanagement. Exzellente Deutschkenntnisse (C2-Niveau), Französischkenntnisse von Vorteil sowie Englischkenntnisse. Eigenständigkeit und kreative Freiheit: Die Möglichkeit, Dich zu beweisen, indem Du selbstständig arbeitest und eigene, innovative Ideen umfassend einbringst als Führungspersönlichkeit. Inklusive Kultur: Arbeiten in einem ambitionierten Team mit regelmäßigem Austausch und Teamveranstaltungen. Mitarbeiterrabatte: Vergünstigte Konditionen auf zahlreiche ausgewählte Markenprodukte und Dienstleistungen über unseren Partner Corporate Benefits. Körperliches Wohlbefinden: Eine subventionierte Mitgliedschaft bei Wellpass, die Deine körperliche Gesundheit unterstützt. Gleiche Chancen Bei Sanoptis schätzen wir Talent, Leidenschaft und Einstellung über spezifische Erfahrungen. Wir begrüßen Bewerber aus verschiedenen Hintergründen und priorisieren gleiche Chancen für alle. title: Infrastructure Engineer (ML Systems) - Paris
description: You’ll own the GPU compute that powers our model training, evaluation and serving systems. This role sits in our Infrastructure team, which works at the lowest layers of our stack, from Kubernetes down to the GPU hardware. You’ll run the clusters, GPUs and schedulers that our research, product and platform teams depend on, and manage the capacity we buy from our cloud providers. What success looks like Success is measured by how well we use our GPUs: keeping production reliable and improving the performance of our training and serving stack. What you’ll be doing Running Kubernetes clusters for GPU training and inference Improving how GPU work is scheduled and placed Detecting, draining and repairing unhealthy GPU nodes Managing capacity with our cloud providers Debugging failures in GPUs, Linux, storage and networking The first year By month 3, you’ll be handling a share of cluster incidents on your own and will have shipped one change to scheduling or node health, such as automatically detecting and draining unhealthy GPU nodes. By month 6, you’ll own one part of the compute layer outright: scheduling and placement, node health and repair, or capacity and new regions. By month 12, you’ll be responsible for a globally distributed GPU system that shifts capacity between training and inference as needs change. Who you’ll work with Your hiring manager is our VP of Engineering. Day to day, you’ll work with the Platform Infrastructure team, the research and product teams who use our compute, and our cloud providers and other vendors. What we think it takes You’re likely a good fit if you: Have built and run GPU workloads on Kubernetes Could design a GPU cluster for training and online RL from scratch Debug confidently at the OS layer and below (Linux, GPU drivers, networking and storage) Write strong Python It’s a plus if you’ve worked as an SRE or infrastructure engineer, or have used: Slurm Kubernetes scheduling and autoscaling tools such as Kueue or Karpenter Multi-cloud orchestration tools such as SkyPilot AWS services such as EKS or SageMaker HyperPod High-performance interconnects and collective communication libraries such as EFA, InfiniBand, NCCL or Open MPI Terraform You don’t need ML research experience. If you match most of this but not every point, please apply. How we hire Four stages, about three hours in total: a 30-minute call with our Talent team, a 60-minute coding interview, a 60-minute system design interview and a closing 30-minute conversation with our VP of Engineering. The coding and system design interviews are modelled on real-world problems you’d face in this role. Practicalities The role is hybrid, with three days a week in our Paris or London office and occasional travel between the two. We offer a competitive package. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Product Designer - Paris
description: As a Product Designer, you'll work on the H Platform, where our users create and run agentic AI workflows powered by our models. Nobody has written the playbook for designing these experiences yet. Our next stage is making the platform truly useful for its users and levelling it up, in design as much as in technology, and you'll build the product experiences that deliver real value in organisations. At H Company, we believe AI should take action in the real world, and our mission is to make agentic AI genuinely useful for large organisations. We're pioneers in computer use: our own vision-language models power agents that see, click and type their way through the software businesses already run, with no integrations or rebuilds, and we own the whole stack, from research and models to the products built on top of them. What you'll be doing Talking to our users constantly to understand their needs and figure out what will make the platform truly useful for them. Turning those insights into research and explorations, looking at problems from different angles before settling on a direction. Picking the right tool for each task: a Figma design, a prototype, or a small PR when a quick change is the fastest way to ship. Testing what you build with users, measuring its impact (A/B testing, user interviews, users daily use data...) and iterating quickly based on what you learn. Shaping the roadmap together with the whole team, engineers and PMs alike. Who you'll work with The role sits in our Product team, which is responsible for product direction, strategy and design. You'll join the product designer who owns design and UX today, and work closely with product, engineering and forward deployed engineers. What we think it takes Above all, we want someone who cares deeply about users, has great product taste and can explain it, moves fast while keeping quality high, leaves their ego at the door and welcomes feedback. Likely a good fit if you Have 5+ years of experience as a Product Designer at tech companies. Have excellent UX, UI and interaction design skills, and can make complex, technical flows, like building and running AI agent workflows, feel simple and intuitive. Have a portfolio that shows your latest work. Have hands-on experience running user tests and A/B tests. Know when a proven solution is good enough and when a problem deserves something new. Have designed complex data or ML/AI-driven products: you know how to make complex systems understandable and how to design for AI behaviour that isn't always predictable, building trust and keeping users in control. Are comfortable in technical discussions: you can dig into constraints and trade-offs with engineers and ramp up quickly on technical topics to discuss them with our researchers and more technical engineers. Are fluent in Figma. Can work within a design system and contribute to it. Stronger still if you Have designed platforms: complex B2B web or desktop software used by professionals, whether that's tools to build and run workflows, big data and analytics software, operational dashboards or other data-dense interfaces. Are curious about code and AI in your design workflow. Every design team is still figuring out how AI changes the way we work, and we're no different, so we'd love someone who has started experimenting, whether by prototyping in code, building small tools or bringing AI into their process, and who wants to keep exploring with us. If you match most of this but not every point, apply anyway. We care far more about how you think, your curiosity and your care for users than a perfect match. How we hire Four stages: a 30-minute call with our Talent team, a 60-minute portfolio review, a 60-minute design interview in person at our Paris office, and a closing 30-minute conversation. The portfolio review and design interview are built around your own work and how you design. Please apply with your CV and a link to your portfolio showing your latest work. title: Research Lead, Predictive Oncology
description: About Orakl Oncology At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. Our research brings together functional treatment-response measurements, molecular profiles and clinical information where available, creating opportunities to investigate how experimental responses translate into patient outcomes. Our platforms are designed to help anticipate clinical trial outcomes, evaluate therapies and identify new therapeutic opportunities. Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology. About the Role We are looking for a Research Lead - Predictive Oncology, to build and lead a research programme to improve the translational capabilities of Orakl Oncology’s platform, and to provide the scientific backbone of O-Predict, Orakl’s predictive solutions. You will own O-Predict's long-term scientific roadmap, choose the questions we pursue, and lead the work needed to answer them. The opportunity combines access to Orakl's experimental and molecular data, clinical information where available, and the ability to shape future data generation with our experimental and clinical collaborators. This is a hands-on scientific leadership role . You will develop and test methods, mentor contributors, and build a coherent body of research with a recognisable scientific contribution. Publications, presentations and external collaborations will be integral outputs of that programme. You will work closely with the CTO and our Data Science, Computational Biology, experimental, product and engineering colleagues. Your research will establish which predictions are reliable, identify their limitations, and inform how O-Predict can support drug-development decisions. The role is suited to a researcher ready to take ownership of an independent programme within a collaborative company, including an emerging research leader with a strong record of original work. What You'll Do Own O-Predict's long-term research roadmap: define and maintain a 2-year scientific agenda, translated into a prioritised 12-month execution plan. Identify the key uncertainties, research hypotheses, data requirements, dependencies and resources; set milestones and explicit criteria for continuing, redirecting or stopping projects. Review priorities with the CTO as evidence and company needs evolve. Lead R&D execution: take research programmes from question formulation through method development, validation and interpretation. Coordinate agreed contributions across Data Science, Computational Biology and experimental teams, establish project ownership, run scientific reviews, resolve blockers and mentor researchers. Remain hands-on in the analyses and modelling decisions that determine scientific quality. Shape future data generation: identify the experiments, measurements and cohorts that would resolve important scientific uncertainties. Co-design these studies with experimental and clinical colleagues, prioritise them within the agreed research allocation, and use the results to test and revise your hypotheses. Advance O-Predict's predictive capabilities: investigate how drug screening, patient-derived models, molecular and clinical data can improve treatment-response and trial-outcome predictions. Assess extensions to new cohorts, indications and therapeutic settings, specifying the evidence needed before extending claims. Own the validation strategy: define relevant endpoints, external baselines and evaluation protocols. Lead independent and prospective validation plans with clinical and experimental collaborators, and document both performance and failure modes. Connect research to product development: work with product and engineering colleagues to translate promising findings into reproducible methods and clearly documented scientific requirements. Define the evidence needed for transfer into O-Predict and assess feasibility, expected value and limitations. Lead publications and scientific materials: build a publication and conference plan around the research roadmap. Lead manuscripts from analysis and figures through submission and reviewer responses, with contributions distributed across the research team. Produce abstracts, posters, talks and methods notes; provide scientific direction and review for partner evidence decks. Build substantive scientific collaborations: work directly with clinical investigators and quantitative researchers to formulate questions, co-design studies, access complementary expertise and pursue independent validation opportunities. Represent O-Predict at relevant oncology and computational conferences, present your team's research, and turn scientific discussions into joint projects and publications. Run publication governance: coordinate authorship and co-author review with hospital and pharmaceutical partners, track contractual publication and acknowledgement obligations, and align disclosure with confidentiality, patient-data permissions and intellectual-property considerations. Minimum Qualifications PhD, PharmD, MD, or MSc with an equivalent research record in a quantitative or biomedical discipline relevant to predictive oncology. Demonstrated ownership of a research programme: you have formulated a scientific agenda, prioritised competing questions and led projects from initial hypothesis to validated findings. Experience leading and mentoring scientific contributors , including coordinating work across disciplines and critically reviewing others' methods and conclusions. A strong publication record in translational oncology, computational biology, biostatistics and/or ML for health , with clear intellectual and analytical contributions. Hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL: you can work with internal data and libraries, develop and evaluate methods, and produce reproducible analyses and figures. Strong grounding in statistical inference, predictive modelling and study design; able to challenge biological assumptions and machine-learning evaluations. Excellent scientific writing and oral communication in English , including manuscripts, scientific presentations and substantive discussions with external researchers. Preferred Qualifications Experience leading R&D in a biotech, health technology or translational research setting, with responsibility for milestones and resource planning. Experience translating research methods into a predictive product or decision-support workflow. Familiarity with patient-derived models, drug sensitivity assays, clinical trial design and oncology endpoints. Experience with independent or prospective validation, multimodal data integration, survival modelling, or pharmacological modelling. Experience establishing academic or clinical collaborations and publishing with pharmaceutical partners. Familiarity with appropriate reporting standards and reproducibility practices, including protocol registration and code and data availability statements. Experience presenting research at oncology or computational conferences and maintaining an active scientific network. Who You Are A scientific owner: you turn an ambitious objective into a focused research agenda and make explicit choices about what deserves the team's time. A hands-on leader: you develop others while staying close enough to the data and code to challenge results and solve difficult problems. Rigorous and intellectually honest: you seek evidence that could disprove your hypotheses, distinguish exploratory findings from validated claims, and report limitations clearly. Curious across disciplines: you connect experimental biology, clinical questions and quantitative methods. An effective collaborator: you build productive relationships, navigate scientific disagreement and turn external discussions into research progress. Why Join Orakl Own a research programme with a clear scientific identity. Shape O-Predict's direction and build a body of work around the translation of experimental treatment responses into clinical predictions. Study a distinctive combination of data. Bring together patient-derived tumor models, functional drug screening and molecular profiles, incorporating clinical information where available. Explore questions that require these modalities to be studied together. Help decide what gets measured next. Work with experimental and clinical colleagues to design new studies that test your ideas and address the limitations of existing data. Work across disciplines every day. Develop methods alongside the scientists generating the measurements, the engineers supporting their use, and collaborators who understand the clinical questions. Build your scientific reputation. Lead original research, manuscripts and conference contributions, and develop sustained collaborations around your programme. Connect discoveries to consequential decisions. Develop and validate methods intended to inform therapy evaluation and clinical development, with a clear account of what the evidence does and does not support. Grow as a research leader. Mentor researchers and help shape the capabilities and future team needed to deliver the programme. Interview Process HR Call: Align on motivation, role scope and expectations. Scientific Deep Dive: Discuss a research programme you led: the questions you chose, your own technical contributions, validation decisions, team leadership and published outcomes. We will share a confidential scientific briefing on O-Predict's current evidence, available data and open questions so you can assess the opportunity. Research Strategy and Analysis Discussion: Using a bounded, representative evidence package, discuss research priorities and a validation plan, critique an analysis, and outline how you would communicate the findings. Meet the experimental and computational colleagues you would work with and discuss the studies you would want to pursue. Reference Call: Speak with one or two close collaborators who can assess scientific judgement, research ownership and leadership. Founder Interview: Discuss O-Predict's scientific direction, decision-making responsibilities, research resources, publication arrangements and mutual ambitions. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Ingénieure ou ingénieur de recherche – Captage du CO₂
description: Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne , c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable . Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain . Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif. L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain. À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École. Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques. Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret. Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité. Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins. L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité. 🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’ industrie du futur. Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ? 🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous En tant qu’ Ingénieur(e), vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affecté au Centre SPIN. Au sein de ce centre, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal afin de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs de neutralité carbone de la France. Le centre SPIN est l’un des centres de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne dédié à la recherche en génie des procédés et rassemble environ 80 personnes comprenant enseignants-chercheurs, postdocs, doctorants, stagiaires, et profite du soutien de personnels administratifs et techniques. L’activité du centre SPIN s’inscrit dans le périmètre du Laboratoire Georges Friedel (UMR 5307) et du Laboratoire Environnement Ville et Société (UMR 5600). Ce recrutement est au cœur de la stratégie d’innovation de Mines Saint-Etienne pour permettre à un brevet IMT de se concrétiser en une technologie permettant de capter le CO2 des fumées industrielles, et de contribuer ainsi à l’atteinte de l’objectif Français de Neutralité carbone · Vous assurez le développement d’un pilote de captage du CO2, · Vous participez au transfert de technologie entre une méthodologie brevetée et la spin-off Carbon Cage, · Vous contribuez à un enjeu majeur de notre société, · Vous rendez compte l’équipe GasHyDyn qui soutient les développements méthodologiques, et vous interagissez au quotidien avec sa spin-off Carbon Cage. Votre capacité à travailler en mode projet et à faire dialoguer recherche et application concrète sera essentielle pour réussir. 🔍 Ce que nous recherchons Vous êtes titulaire d’un : · Diplôme Bac + 5 ou équivalent, Et idéalement : · Titulaire d’une thèse · Junior accepté : [oui] • Une expérience significative sur le domaine des clathrates hydrates • Une maîtrise de l’anglais (niveau C1) Vos atouts supplémentaires : • Capacité à travailler dans un contexte international et multiculturel • Capacité à travailler avec une startup 🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne ? Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde . Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est l’opportunité de trouver : · Un environnement stimulant : des moyens expérimentaux de pointe, un réseau international solide (T.I.M.E., EULIST) et des campus à taille humaine avec un environnement urbain · Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an · Une qualité de vie incomparable : 49 jours de congés et RTT, télétravail partiel, prise en charge des transports en commun à 75 %, soutien financier au covoiturage et au vélo et un baromètre social où 83 % des collaborateurs plébiscitent la qualité de vie au travail. Construisons un avenir plus durable, à travers la science , l’ ingénierie , et des projets qui font sens . 📩 Candidatez dès maintenant ! Date limite de candidature : 12/11/2026 🔗 Les dossiers de candidature (CV, lettre de motivation, lettre de recommandation le cas échéant, pièce d’identité) sont à déposer sur la plateforme RECRUITEE : https://institutminestelecom.recruitee.com/o/ingenieure-ou-ingenieur-de-recherche-captage-du-co Dans le cadre de sa politique Égalité, Diversité et Inclusion, l’École des Mines de Saint Etienne est un employeur soucieux de l’équité de traitement entre les candidatures. Informations complémentaires · Date de prise de poste souhaitée : 01/02/2027 · Rémunération fixée selon le profil du candidat, en fonction des règles définies par le cadre de gestion de l’Institut Mines Télécom. · Les postes offerts au recrutement sont ouverts à toutes et tous avec, sur demande, des aménagements pour les candidates et candidats en situation de handicap. · Emploi ouvert aux personnes contractuelles · A moyen terme un poste pérenne est susceptible d’être ouvert · Toute candidature peut faire l’objet d’une enquête administrative · A usage interne Institut Mines Télécom : Ø Catégorie II – Métier P – Post-doctorant selon le Cadre de Gestion 📞 Contacts · Sur le contenu du poste : Mathilde Rieu _ Enseignant-Chercheur Mail : · Sur les aspects administratifs/RH: Milica PETKOVIC– Gestionnaire RH Mail : Tel. : + 33 (0)4 77 42 02 08 Liens utiles : Ecole : https://www.mines-stetienne.fr/ IMT : La protection de vos données : https://www.mines-stetienne.fr/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Informations-des-candidats-sur-les-traitements-de-donn%C3%A9es-personnelles.pdf etienne.fr/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Informations-des-candidats-sur-les-traitements-de-donn%C3%A9es-personnelles.pdf Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Distributed Systems Engineer - Cache
description: <div class="content-intro"><h3>About Us</h3> <p>At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.</p> <p>At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.</p></div><p><strong>Available Locations: Atlanta, GA, Austin, TX, Champaign, IL, New York, NY, San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA, Washington, DC</strong></p> <h2>About the Department</h2> <p>Cloudflare's Engineering Team builds and runs the software that helps power millions of Internet properties. Product development covers both new features and functionality as well as scaling our existing software to meet the challenges of a massively growing customer base.</p> <p>The Content Delivery group helps make the Internet faster, safer, and more reliable by building and optimizing one of the world's largest CDNs.</p> <h2>Role Summary</h2> <p>The Cache team builds and operates the high-performance reverse proxy and caching data plane at Cloudflare's edge. Built on Pingora, Cloudflare's open-source Rust framework for fast, reliable network services, this software serves cached content, routes traffic across cache tiers, and connects Cloudflare to customer origins. Its performance, correctness, and resilience directly affect request latency, origin load, and availability across Cloudflare's global network.</p> <p>You will work primarily on the reverse proxy and the services that support it: backend routing and load balancing, cache storage and indexing, globally distributed purge, Tiered Cache routing, and production observability. These systems are also foundational building blocks for teams across Cloudflare, which use the proxy, caching, routing, and purge capabilities to power their own products. The team carries these capabilities through shared internal interfaces, distributed control planes, and customer-facing products including Cache Rules, Tiered Cache, Cache Reserve, Workers Cache API, and Always Online. Features ship end to end: you will help design, implement, test, roll out, and operate the systems you build.</p> <p>This is a good fit if you enjoy problems where latency, correctness, and reliability are hard requirements; where changes must be introduced safely across a global fleet; and where improvements can benefit a significant portion of Internet traffic.</p> <h2>Role Responsibilities</h2> <ul> <li>Design, build, and operate the high-performance cache and proxy data plane that serves content at Cloudflare's edge and connects to customer origins</li> <li>Contribute to Pingora and the production services built on it, improving asynchronous I/O, connection handling, memory and disk efficiency, and tail latency</li> <li>Improve cache correctness and performance through object placement, retention, admission and eviction policies, range-request handling, and resilience to corrupt or incomplete data</li> <li>Build globally distributed purge and Tiered Cache systems that invalidate content quickly, select efficient cache paths, improve hit rates, and reduce origin load</li> <li>Deliver shared platform capabilities and customer-facing APIs and rules for cache keys, TTLs, response handling, purge behavior, and programmatic access from Workers</li> <li>Own features end to end: write technical designs, implement services and libraries, add automated tests and observability, drive staged rollouts, and operate the resulting systems in production</li> <li>Participate in the team's on-call rotation, lead incident response and post-mortems, and continually improve reliability, capacity, and operational tooling</li> <li>Reason carefully about failure modes and blast radius, using traffic cohorts, measurable guardrails, and rollback mechanisms to introduce high-impact changes safely</li> <li>Partner with product and engineering teams across Cloudflare that depend on or extend the cache and proxy platform</li> <li>Raise the engineering bar through code review, mentorship, clear written communication, and improvements to team standards and tooling</li> </ul> <h2>Role Requirements (Must-Have Skills)</h2> <ul> <li>Minimum 4 years of professional experience designing, building, and operating production software systems</li> <li>Strong proficiency in at least one systems or backend language such as Rust, Go, C, or C++, with a willingness to work in Rust</li> <li>Strong understanding of HTTP semantics and transport protocols such as TCP, TLS, and QUIC</li> <li>Experience designing and implementing secure, resilient, high-performance distributed systems</li> <li>Experience with Linux systems, networking, concurrency, and performance analysis</li> <li>Track record of production ownership, including monitoring, debugging, on-call, incident response, and ongoing reliability improvements</li> <li>Experience using metrics, logs, traces, profiling, and experiments to understand production behavior and validate improvements</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write clear technical designs and lead projects across team boundaries</li> <li>Willingness to use AI-assisted engineering tools to accelerate development and investigation while remaining accountable for correctness, security, and design quality</li> </ul> <h2>Nice-to-Have Skills</h2> <ul> <li>Professional experience with Rust or high-performance asynchronous systems</li> <li>Experience with caches, HTTP proxies, CDNs, distributed storage, or latency-sensitive data-plane services</li> <li>Experience analyzing memory use, disk I/O, resource contention, and tail latency in production systems</li> <li>Experience building APIs or distributed control planes using event streaming, relational databases, or analytical data systems</li> <li>Familiarity with Kubernetes, Kafka, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, or similar infrastructure</li> <li>Experience contributing to open-source software or leading multi-team engineering programs</li> </ul> <p><strong>Compensation</strong></p> <p>Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location and level.</p> <p>San Francisco Estimated Base salary $194,000 - $266,000.</p> <p>Seattle, Washington D.C., New York Estimated Base salary $185,000 - $254,000.</p> <p>Austin, Illinois, Atlanta Estimated Base salary $168,000 - $231,000.</p> <p><strong>Equity</strong></p> <p>This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h3>What Makes Cloudflare Special?</h3> <p><span We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.</span></p> <p><a href="https://blog.cloudflare.com/protecting-free-expression-online/"><strong>Project Galileo</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.</span></p> <p><strong><a href="https://www.cloudflare.com/athenian/">Athenian Project</a></strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.</span></p> <p><a href="https://1.1.1.1/"><strong>1.1.1.1</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">: We released</span><a href="https://1.1.1.1/"> <span style="font-weight: 400;">1.1.1.1</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. title: Sr. Product Manager - ClickStack
description: ClickHouse is looking for a Product Manager to join the ClickStack team and own major parts of the product end to end. This is a hands-on product role. You’ll work directly with customers, use and instrument the product yourself, develop a deep understanding of the underlying systems, and turn that understanding into a shipped product. Initial focus areas are likely to include ClickStack onboarding and cloud workflows, alerting, and the broader telemetry ingestion and integration ecosystem. What you’ll do Own major observability product areas from customer discovery through product definition, delivery, adoption, and iteration. Take ownership of areas such as alerting, anomaly detection, onboarding, provisioning, and telemetry integrations. Work directly with customers and prospects to understand observability use cases, migration requirements, operational workflows, and emerging needs. Improve the end-to-end onboarding experience, including getting telemetry into ClickStack, configuring the product, and migrating from existing observability platforms. Drive integrations across the observability ecosystem, including OpenTelemetry and common cloud, infrastructure, and logging sources. Act as user 0. Set up environments yourself, instrument applications, send telemetry, reproduce customer workflows, and use the product at a meaningful scale. Work closely with engineering and design, including prototyping workflows yourself when useful rather than relying exclusively on written requirements. Design end-to-end observability experiences with both engineers and AI agents as first-class users. Coordinate broadly across teams and products where ClickStack depends on or integrates with other parts of the ClickHouse ecosystem and external products. Work across product boundaries to shape cohesive experiences spanning ClickStack, ClickHouse Cloud, and complementary products and integrations. Stay close to customers after shipping and use adoption, product data, and direct feedback to determine what needs to improve next. What you bring Experience driving an observability product or platform in a similar-stage or later-stage company. A proven track record of shipping successful products in the observability SaaS space. Strong technical depth. You’re comfortable moving from a user workflow into telemetry pipelines, APIs, schemas, queries, databases, and infrastructure when necessary. A hands-on working style. You’re comfortable deploying software, instrumenting applications, debugging integrations, querying data, and ideally building prototypes or contributing code. Strong product judgment and the ability to turn ambiguous customer problems into concrete product decisions. Comfort working directly with technical users and enterprise customers, including during migrations and complex evaluations. Comfort operating in a dynamic environment where priorities, ownership boundaries, and the problems that need attention can change quickly. Strong written and verbal communication with engineering, design, customers, field teams, and leadership. Experience working with and enabling a large and diverse sales team, supporting enterprise customers and complex sales cycles. Experience engaging with open source communities, including managing community expectations and incorporating community-driven input and contributions. Familiarity with OpenTelemetry and the broader observability ecosystem. Perks Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries. Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare. Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options. Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries. A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee. Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites. Culture - We All Shape It As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture. Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here . Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse. title: Embedded System Lead Engineer
description: Pelagon - Autonomous Maritime ISR Full-time · On-site (Marseille or Paris) · Founding team · Reports to founders The sea is the physical layer of the economy—the conduit for our energy, communications, and trade. It is also Europe’s exposed flank. Pelagon is building the answer. Founded by Aymeric (serial deeptech entrepreneur; founded & exited Scortex, Leading AI solution for manufacturing quality) and Gauthier (Navy officer and McKinsey), Pelagon is building a foundational multimodal acoustic model for autonomous maritime protection (underwater and surface) in service of European sovereignty. It will be deployed on a distributed, autonomous network of vectors (UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys, seabed…) to provide real-time understanding of underwater threats. France and Europe have world-class acoustic engineers and a long history in underwater warfare. By bridging this expertise with modern physical-AI strategies (as seen in autonomous driving and robotics). Europe is still missing it’s naval NeoPrime, Pelagon aims to become to lead the way in autonomous marine protection—from detection to interception—partnering with leading navies, primes, and neo-primes, while also operating its own fleet as a service. Pelagon is backed by Hexa , the pioneer startup studio in Europe, which has launched 35+ companies, including unicorns like Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, combining €230m+ ARR and €750m raised. The role As Embedded System Lead Engineer , you take end-to-end technical ownership of the hardware, electronics, and embedded stack across a small family of autonomous maritime platforms, some operating on the surface, some beneath it. What they share matters more than what sets them apart: each must persist at sea for long stretches, sense its surroundings, run our AI on-device, and report back intelligently — all while surviving a brutal environment on a very tight energy budget. You will lead their technical development , from architecture and component selection through bring-up, integration, sea trials, and iteration. You'll set the engineering bar for the platforms team and shape how we build for years to come. These platforms exist to carry one thing into the water: our AI. Pelagon trains high-performance detection models in-house on its own stack, and those models have to run on-device, at the edge , on a razor-thin power budget — then push results back to our operations center. Designing the compute-and-power architecture that makes this possible is the heart of the role. The mandate is simple and uncompromising: get reliable hardware in the water fast, and start collecting data. Every week of persistent at-sea operation compounds. The hardware is the gate to all of it. What you'll own Common system architecture across the platforms: power, sensing, compute, and communications. The edge-AI compute platform — selecting and integrating the processors and accelerators that run our in-house detection models on-device, and extracting maximum inference from every milliwatt. Electronics design and integration — power distribution, battery systems, motor/thruster control, sensor interfaces (acoustic, pressure, IMU, GNSS, AIS). The embedded software and autopilot stack, firmware, and the low-level glue that makes autonomy reliable in a brutal, wet, salty environment. Robustness and efficiency engineering: watertight integrity, power budgets and endurance, thermal behaviour, EMC, and graceful failure modes far from shore. Hands-on bring-up and sea trials — you'll be on the dock and on the boat, not just at the bench. Vendor and component decisions, and the build-up of our test and manufacturing practices as we scale from prototype to fielded units. The hard problems you'll be solving These are genuinely difficult, and that's the point: Persistence with a finite power budget. Endurance is everything for a surveillance node — squeezing weeks of useful operation out of a sealed, ship-deployable platform is a relentless optimization problem across power, compute, and duty-cycling. Reliability with no one to fix it. A system at sea has to fail safe and recover on its own. There is no field technician at 30 nm offshore in a 2 m swell. Running real AI at the edge, on almost no power. This is the defining challenge of the role. Our in-house models have to run inference on-device, in real time, on platforms with a razor-thin energy budget — then sense, sleep, and wake intelligently to stretch endurance from hours into weeks. Getting high-performance ML to live within milliwatts is what makes the entire system possible. Sensing in a hostile medium. The ocean fights you at every turn — pressure, corrosion, biofouling, acoustic noise, intermittent comms — and the hardware has to keep sensing and computing through all of it. Speed without fragility. We are building fast toward sea trials, but a demonstrator that breaks doesn't generate data. You'll have to find the line between moving quickly and building things that survive the ocean. Who we're looking for You are a sharp, senior builder who wants to own a problem, not be handed a ticket. Specifically: 5+ years building real, shipping hardware — embedded systems that had to be efficient, robust, and survive the real world. Direct experience building drones or autonomous systems . This could come from drone companies (e.g. Parrot), automotive / autonomous vehicles, or the marine autonomy space. Deep, hands-on command of the full embedded stack : electronics design, power systems, motor/actuator control, sensor integration, microcontrollers and embedded Linux, and firmware close to the metal. Comfort with autopilot / flight-controller ecosystems (Pixhawk, ArduPilot / ArduSub / PX4 or equivalent) and the realities of real-time control. Experience deploying AI/ML models at the edge — embedded inference, accelerators (GPU / NPU / TPU-class), model quantization and optimization, and the power-versus-performance tradeoffs that come with it. This is central to what we do. A bias toward action: you prototype, test, break, and iterate — and you're energized by tight deadlines and a mission that genuinely matters. Fluency working in a fast, ambiguous, founding-team environment where you define the process as much as follow it. Bonus points for: mechanical / mechatronic breadth (you can reason about hulls, sealing, and thrust as well as circuits); experience with subsea or marine hardware; comms in degraded / contested environments; CFD or hydrodynamics intuition; or having taken a hardware product from zero to fielded at scale. Why join now Founding ownership. You'll be one of the first engineers and will define the technical foundation of the company. Meaningful equity comes with that. A mission with weight. This is hardware that protects critical infrastructure and Europe's maritime space. Real things, in the real ocean, fast. You'll see your work in the water within weeks, not years. AI-first, at the edge, in the real world. We train our own models and run them where it counts: in the water, on the device. You'll be solving the edge-ML and power problems most companies only talk about. A sovereign, European deeptech at the inflection point of a market with strong NATO and EU policy momentum behind it. They should also be astute judges of character, and comfortable setting expectations and holding colleagues accountable to them. </p> <p>We are building an observability stack that is easy to deploy and operate on Kubernetes. This is part of a broader initiative to deliver the world's best suite of open source tools, where we provide deep integration and automation for best-of-breed open source offerings that cover metrics, logging, telemetry, alerting, tracing and profiling. Our goal is to make observability tools integral and pervasive across software practices .</p> <p>Our implementation of Kubernetes operators is opinionated, resilient, and scalable, providing deep insights out of the box. The user experience is polished and seamless for the end-users, and its administrators will enjoy smooth, lightweight Day 1 and Day 2 operations. We are excited to be improving the state of the art for open-source observability.</p> <p>This is an exciting opportunity for a software engineer passionate about open source software, Linux, Kubernetes, and Observability. Observability Stack</li> </ul> <h2>What we are looking for in you</h2> <ul> <li>An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university</li> <li>A proven track record of professional experience of software delivery</li> <li>Professional software development experience, preferably with a track record in open source</li> <li>Willingness to travel up to 4 times a year for internal events</li> <li>Professional written and spoken English </li> <li>Experience with Linux (Debian or Ubuntu preferred) </li> <li>Excellent interpersonal skills, curiosity, flexibility, and accountability </li> <li>Passion, thoughtfulness, and self-motivation </li> <li>Excellent communication and presentation skills </li> <li>Result-oriented, with a personal drive to meet commitments</li> </ul> <h2>Nice-to-have skills</h2> <ul> <li>Experience as an engineering manager, with a track record of building great, high performance teams  </li> <li>Professional Python development experience</li> <li>A working knowledge of Go</li> <li>Open source contribution experience</li> <li>Interest and experience with container technologies</li> <li>A proven understanding of the importance of observability and monitoring for keeping software running smoothly</li> <li>Experience designing and implementing observability solutions</li> </ul> <h2>What we offer colleagues</h2> <p>We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.</p> <ul> <li>Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person</li> <li>Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year</li> <li>Annual compensation review</li> <li>Recognition rewards</li> <li>Annual holiday leave</li> <li>Maternity and paternity leave</li> <li>Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform</li> <li>Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues</li> <li>Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events</li> </ul> <h2>About Canonical</h2> <p>Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. title: Power Electronics Engineer
description: WHO WE ARE Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant. Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach. Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions. BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO Architect a breakthrough energy technology – Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy. Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion – Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion. YOUR IMPACT Join our team to work on cutting-edge power conversion technologies, developing solutions that combine high power density, high voltage and current, fast dynamic response, and demanding efficiency and reliability requirements. In this role, you will translate functional and system requirements into robust power-stage solutions. Your work will contribute to optimizing efficiency, thermal performance, reliability, scalability, and power density. You will work closely with colleagues across integrated electronics, embedded software, mechanical, thermal, and system engineering. WHAT YOU WILL DO Evaluate and develop power conversion topologies for converters, considering performance, efficiency, electrical stresses, thermal behaviour, reliability, power density, and system requirements. Design and develop magnetic components such as inductors, transformers, and chokes, including selection of magnetic materials, core geometries, winding concepts, and evaluation of losses and thermal limitations. Develop analytical and simulation models to evaluate converter behaviour, semiconductor stresses, switching and conduction losses, efficiency, and performance across relevant operating conditions. Build prototypes and perform laboratory testing, characterization, verification, troubleshooting, and validation of power electronic circuits and converter stages. Analyse test results and correlate measurements with simulations and calculations to identify design improvements and validate converter performance. WHO YOU ARE You hold a University (Higher education) degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or a related field. You are experienced in taking power-stage designs from initial concept and simulation through component selection, prototype implementation, laboratory measurement, debugging, and validation. You are an expert in power conversion topologies, power semiconductors, magnetic components, and passive components. Experience with electro-thermal simulation tools such as PLECS is a plus. Experience with SiC or GaN semiconductors, high-frequency magnetics is a plus. INTERVIEW PROCESS Recruiter Interview (30-60 min) Technical Screening (30 min) Technical Panel (3x60 min) At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table. Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

title: Solutions Architecture Lead
description: AMPECO is one of the most innovative companies in the area of electric vehicle charging infrastructure - an industry that aims to change the world by making charging easier for everyone. As electric vehicles (EVs) drive a transformation of the transport and mobility sectors, AMPECO is at the forefront of that grand revolution, and we’re just getting started. Our product - the AMPECO EV Charging Platform - is a business-critical SaaS platform used by companies to manage their EV charging infrastructure, processes and energy use. It’s already in use by companies all over the world, from North and South America to Europe, Asia and Australia. Our team is highly motivated, capable, and committed to our mission. We are looking to expand it with like-minded, capable people, eager to give, learn and grow with us. About the Role As a Solutions Architecture Lead at AMPECO you will be a senior individual contributor who guides customers through the architecture, design, and delivery of complex technical projects, from the first conversation to a successful project go-live. You will work on specific engagements and can join as early as the pre-sales stage. With a new prospect, you will help define the overall solution architecture and migration strategy. You will also own the planning, estimation, and risk assessment that support bidding and contracting. Once a prospect becomes an AMPECO customer, you will lead their onboarding and migration. When the project is complete, you will hand them over smoothly to a business-as-usual setup. As existing customers take on new integrations or complex initiatives, you might again lead the planning and delivery. Why this role matters This role is highly visible and carries real technical authority. You will be the senior strategic and technical voice for customers at the most critical point in their relationship with AMPECO. We are looking for someone who is equally confident in business and technical conversations, and who can turn complex requirements into clear, achievable plans. If you are based in France, have a passion for e-mobility alongside a combination of deep technical grounding and strong client-facing presence, read on to find out more about our opportunity. What we are looking for Client-facing experience Experience in a technical consulting, solutions engineering, or client delivery role - ideally in e-mobility, B2B SaaS or infrastructure software Proven ability to manage multiple client engagements simultaneously - prioritising, communicating status, and delivering without dropping threads Comfortable running workshops and enablement sessions for varied audiences - technical and non-technical alike Skilled at translating ambiguous client needs into concrete, actionable technical plans Fluent English plus French and/or German Availability to travel and meet prospects and customers on a regular basis Technical skills Hands-on experience with REST API integrations Confidence with network and connectivity troubleshooting - firewalls, TLS certificates, WebSocket connections Cloud infrastructure awareness and ability to understand how SaaS platforms are structured and where failures propagate Programming knowledge enabling you to read code, use and contribute to internal tools, and confidently use AI to script solutions that make your work more efficient Working style High ownership mentality - you take problems all the way to resolution Structured and systematic - you document as you go and leave things better than you found them Collaborative - you involve the right people early, and share what you learn across the team Calm under pressure - escalations and urgent situations sharpen your focus rather than scatter it. Considered an advantage Familiarity with eRoaming hubs - Hubject, Gireve, or similar Experience leading or supporting data migration projects Familiarity with Energy Management Additional language skills What we offer A seat at a fast-growing company on the path to becoming a global industry leader Opportunity to work and grow with a highly specialised team of experts who genuinely enjoy working together on the most interesting projects in a high-impact industry Flexibility to work from anywhere in France Attractive employee package Our team at AMPECO is deeply committed to our mission and we're looking for like-minded individuals eager to give, learn and grow with us. If you're passionate about innovative technology and want to make a real impact in the e-mobility sector, we want to hear from you. Join AMPECO in building the future of EV charging! Our interview process is entirely remote. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: IA Engineer Intern (x/f/m) - Paris
description: <p>Join a team of passionate and committed people working to improve healthcare.</p> <p>At Doctolib, our tech teams build products and features that improve the daily lives of healthcare professionals and patients. We work in feature teams within an agile environment, in close collaboration with Product, Design, Data Science, and Business teams.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <p>We are looking for an <strong>AI Engineer Intern</strong> to join our Tech team and contribute to the development of AI-powered features at Doctolib.</p> <p>You will work closely with experienced AI and software engineers to explore, prototype, evaluate, and improve AI-based solutions. This internship will give you the opportunity to gain practical experience across the different stages of an AI product, from experimentation to integration into a production environment.</p> <p>Your responsibilities will include:</p> <ul> <li>Contribute to the development of AI features and services under the guidance of experienced engineers</li> <li>Write Python code to support prototypes, experiments, evaluation tools, and backend components</li> <li>Experiment with large language models, prompting techniques, retrieval, and tool integration</li> <li>Contribute to automated tests and documentation for the components you develop</li> <li>Investigate issues, analyse results, and suggest improvements to your team</li> <li>Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and team rituals</li> </ul> <p>You will receive regular guidance from your mentor and teammates. The scope of your work will grow progressively as you become familiar with the codebase, the tools, and the technical challenges.</p> <h2><strong>Who you are</strong></h2> <p>Before you read on, if you do not have the exact profile described below but feel that this internship matches your skills and interests, we still encourage you to apply.</p> <p>You will be a great fit if you:</p> <ul> <li>Are in the final year of a degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, or a related field</li> <li>Have basic experience with Python through coursework, personal projects, research, or previous internships</li> <li>Have a basic understanding of programming concepts, data structures, and software development</li> <li>Are curious about artificial intelligence and interested in understanding how AI systems work</li> <li>Are comfortable communicating in English, both written and spoken</li> </ul> <p>It would be fantastic if you:</p> <ul> <li>Have worked on a project involving machine learning, natural language processing, or large language models</li> <li>Have used agentic frameworks like Langchain or Google ADK.</li> <li>Have experimented with AI APIs, prompting, retrieval, or conversational interfaces</li> <li>Have experience in taking products to production and supporting them with real users.</li> <li>Have some experience with Git, APIs, testing, or data analysis</li> <li>Have an interest in healthcare, privacy, or responsible AI</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Life at Doctolib Tech</strong></h2> <p>Our products are built on a cloud-native platform that supports web and mobile applications across several countries and healthcare systems.</p> <p>Even if Doctolib uses technologies like Ruby on Rails, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Swift, React Native, and many cloud-related technologies, the principal language you'll work on is Python.You will also have the opportunity to use AI-assisted development tools within our engineering practices.</p> <p>Discover our AI vision<a href="https://careers.doctolib.com/ai-careers/"> here</a> and learn more about our tech culture on the<a href="https://careers.doctolib.com/tech-doctolib/"> Doctolib Tech site</a>.</p> <h2><strong>What we offer</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A structured internship with dedicated mentoring</li> <li>The opportunity to work on real AI projects in a healthcare environment</li> <li>Technical learning sessions and access to internal engineering communities</li> <li>Access to AI tools for coding, development, and learning</li> <li>Meal vouchers</li> <li>Free breakfast in the office</li> <li>Up to 2 days of remote work per week</li> <li>A flexible workplace policy, depending on the team and location</li> <li>A collaborative and international working environment</li> </ul> <h2><strong>The interview process</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Coding Game</li> <li>Recruiter Interview</li> <li>Technical Interview</li> <li>Behavioral Interview</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Job details</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Internship, 6 months, full-time</li> <li>Location: Berlin, Paris, Nantes, Milan, or Amsterdam</li> <li>Hybrid work setup, up to 2 remote days per week</li> <li>Start date: March 2027</li> </ul> <h2><strong>We welcome everyone</strong></h2> <p>At Doctolib, we are committed to improving access to healthcare for everyone. We evaluate candidates based on their qualifications, motivation, and potential, without discrimination.</p> <p>The more diverse ideas are heard, the better our products can serve patients and healthcare professionals. description: <div data-page-number="1"> <div class="react-pdf__Page shadow-md" data-page-number="1"> <div class="react-pdf__Page__textContent textLayer selecting" data-main-rotation="0"> <h2><strong>Vos missions</strong></h2> </div> <div class="react-pdf__Page__annotations annotationLayer" data-main-rotation="0"> <p class="p3">Notre équipe Finance SSC (Shared Service Center) réinvente la comptabilité chez Doctolib. Là où la plupart des entreprises commencent à peine à mentionner l'IA dans leurs fiches de poste comptables, nous l'intégrons déjà au cœur de nos processus. Nous sommes en avance sur le marché — et nous assumons cette ambition.<br><br>Nous recherchons un(e) General Accountant Lead & Analyst pour rejoindre l'équipe General Ledger (GL). Ce rôle est bien plus qu'un poste de comptable senior : vous couvrirez l'intégralité des flux d'activités courantes (cycles fournisseurs, clients, immobilisations), avec un fort degré de reporting transverse en clôture, tout en portant un œil critique de contrôle de gestion sur les opérations. Vous serez à la fois garant(e) de la qualité des comptes, pilote de la transformation IA de l'équipe et business partner pour les directions Finance et opérationnelles.<br><br>Si vous cherchez un poste où la comptabilité rime avec impact stratégique, transformation digitale et leadership — ce rôle est fait pour vous.</p> <p class="p3"><strong>Vos responsabilités incluent, mais ne sont pas limitées à :</strong></p> <ul class="ul1"> <li class="li3">Piloter l'ensemble des cycles comptables courants (fournisseurs, clients, immobilisations, charges) et garantir leur fiabilité à l'échelle du groupe, en intégrant systématiquement une revue analytique de type contrôle de gestion (Réel vs Budget/N-1, détection d'anomalies, anticipation des impacts P&L)</li> <li class="li3">Orchestrer les processus de clôture de bout en bout dans une posture de « tour de contrôle » : coordination inter-équipes, reporting transverse, allocation analytique des coûts, contrôle interne et documentation SOX intégrés au quotidien</li> <li class="li3">Identifier et piloter des projets de transformation digitale et IA (agents Dust, solutions R2R, RPA) et construire des livrables autoportés (dashboards accompagner l'internationalisation</li> <li class="li3">Incarner la posture de business partner en traduisant les enjeux comptables en langage business et en assurant une veille réglementaire active</li> </ul> <p> </p> <h2><strong>Les qualités attendues pour ce poste</strong></h2> <p class="p1">Avant de poursuivre votre lecture, si vous n'avez pas le profil exact décrit ci-dessous, mais que vous pensez que cette description de poste correspond à vos compétences et à vos aspirations, nous vous encourageons tout de même à postuler.</p> <p class="p1"><strong>Vous pourrez être le/la prochain(e) membre de notre équipe si vous :</strong></p> <ul class="ul1"> <li class="li1">Disposez d'une formation supérieure en Comptabilité/Finance (DSCG, Master CCA, Grande École, DEC en cours ou obtenu)</li> <li class="li1">Justifiez de 8 à 10 ans d'expérience en comptabilité générale et/ou audit, dont au moins 3 ans en position de management ou de leadership technique</li> <li class="li1">Avez une expérience significative en Big 4 (Manager/Senior Manager) et/ou en entreprise internationale en forte croissance</li> <li class="li1">Maîtrisez les normes IFRS (dont IFRS 16, 15) et French GAAP, et avez une expérience approfondie des environnements SOX</li> <li class="li1">Faites preuve d'un esprit analytique fort et d'une capacité à intégrer une démarche de contrôle de gestion dans votre pratique comptable</li> <li class="li1">Êtes à l'aise avec les ERP modernes et maîtrisez Excel/Google Sheets à un niveau avancé</li> <li class="li1">Parlez anglais couramment (C1/C2) — échanges quotidiens avec les équipes internationales</li> <li class="li1">Êtes un(e) leader naturel(le), capable de fédérer, mentorer et conduire le changement</li> </ul> <p class="p2"> </p> <p class="p1"><strong>Ce serait fantastique si vous aviez aussi :</strong></p> <ul class="ul1"> <li class="li1">Une expérience dans le secteur Tech/SaaS et/ou en environnement multi-pays</li> <li title: Engineering Team Lead, Serverless Containers
description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The team Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all. We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write. European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it. The Role This is a people-leadership role from day one. You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad. If you are looking for a senior IC role, this is not it. You will lead the team building our serverless containers product: the way developers run AI apps, MCP servers, APIs, and managed workers on our cloud without thinking about servers. Push a container, get an endpoint, scale from zero to thousands of instances and back down — across CPU and GPU. On a hyperscaler, the serverless layer is a product someone else built. Here you own it end to end: the scheduler that decides where a container lands, the routing path a request takes, the machinery that turns a scaled-to-zero service into a warm instance before a customer notices. All of it runs on metal, network, and datacenters we own. That tension is the product: scale-to-zero economics with cold starts in milliseconds, autoscaling that absorbs a launch spike without a config change, GPUs scheduled onto containers the way other platforms schedule CPU. The customers betting on this layer are the developers building the next generation of AI software on European infrastructure. What You Will Do Own the container platform end to end: image delivery, placement, request routing, scale-up, scale-to-zero — across CPU and GPU. Make cold starts a solved problem: snapshotting, prewarming, image-layer caching, whatever it takes for scale-from-zero to feel instant. Treat AI workloads as the normal case: GPU-backed containers, streaming responses, long-lived connections, MCP servers that cost almost nothing while idle. Write Go alongside your team and own the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions. Grow the engineers, not just the software — set the standard for ownership and coach people past their comfort zone. Own people management for the team: hiring, performance, growth paths, and honest feedback. Partner with Product Managers to turn platform decisions into a product developers want to deploy on. What We're Looking For 2+ years of real people leadership. You have managed engineers — hired, coached, given honest feedback, and grown them. Hands-on contribution matters here, but this role is judged on the team you build and lead, not just the code you write. You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped. You have built container or workload platforms — orchestration, scheduling, isolation, request routing — not just deployed onto someone else's serverless platform. Deep Linux: namespaces, cgroups, image layers, page cache — comfortable well below the application layer. Multi-tenancy instincts: density, isolation, and fairness when hundreds of customers share one fleet. Significant experience building complex backend or infrastructure systems. You have partnered with product, design, and business teams to ship software that reached real users. A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside. Poser des questions sur le fonctionnement de chaque entreprise et recommander des solutions adaptées en matière de paiement, de matériel, de caisse et de logiciels. Gérer le processus de vente depuis le premier échange, en passant par les démonstrations de produits, la gestion des objections et la conclusion, dans le cadre du partenariat. Aider les clients à mettre en place et à commencer à utiliser leurs produits SumUp. Établir des relations avec les chefs d'entreprise et demander des recommandations aux clients satisfaits. Planifier vos visites et vos suivis afin d'optimiser votre temps sur le terrain. Suivre votre activité, vos opportunités et vos résultats de vente, et transmettre les informations nécessaires au traitement des ventes. Échanger avec votre interlocuteur SumUp pour bénéficier de son expertise produit et de conseils commerciaux. Ce que nous recherchons Indispensable Au moins un an d'expérience dans la vente sur le terrain dans des secteurs tels que les télécommunications, l'énergie, les technologies d'entreprise, la gestion des déchets, les systèmes de sécurité ou l'approvisionnement en produits alimentaires et boissons. Une expérience de la prospection à froid, notamment en démarchant des entreprises en face à face et en trouvant vos propres prospects. Une expérience de la vente auprès de petites et moyennes entreprises et des relations directes avec les propriétaires ou les décideurs. Des résultats démontrables en matière d'acquisition de nouveaux clients et d'atteinte d'objectifs commerciaux. Nous vous demanderons des exemples de vos réalisations et de la manière dont vous y êtes parvenu. La capacité à gérer un processus de vente de la première prise de contact à la conclusion, y compris la gestion des questions et des objections. Un bon sens de l'organisation et un suivi rigoureux. La capacité à gérer les refus, à tirer les leçons des retours d'expérience et à persévérer. Une bonne compréhension du statut d'indépendant et la volonté de développer votre portefeuille de clients. La capacité à vous déplacer sur votre territoire de vente afin de rencontrer régulièrement vos prospects et clients. Atouts Un réseau existant de chefs d'entreprise locaux susceptibles de bénéficier des produits SumUp. Une expérience dans le domaine des paiements, des services aux commerçants ou des systèmes de point de vente. Une expérience de la vente par téléphone est un atout, mais vous devez également avoir vendu en face à face sur le terrain. Rémunération Il s'agit d'une activité indépendante, rémunérée exclusivement à la commission, sans salaire de base ni revenu minimum garanti. Les commissions sont déplafonnées et dépendent de vos résultats commerciaux et de l'activité des commerçants apportés. Le système de commissions comprend, dans le cadre des conditions Partner : Paiements : 50 % du revenu net annualisé lié aux transactions. Matériel : 50 % du prix de vente retenu dans le barème. Logiciels et abonnements : 50 % du montant annuel retenu dans le barème. Revenu résiduel : 20 % du revenu net mensuel généré par les commerçants apportés, pendant une durée maximale de trois ans. Avantage de bienvenue : trois fois le montant habituel des commissions résiduelles pendant les trois premiers mois. Primes supplémentaires liées à certains produits ou opérations commerciales. Les commissions s'entendent avant déduction de vos frais professionnels, cotisations sociales et impôts applicables.
